summary: Pinned model version lost when canary shifts to spot GPU nodes causing automatic fallback to quantized variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a scheduled canary traffic shift the pinned model version (redwood-13b-v2) for their route was unintentionally lost after the cluster autoscaler replaced two canary nodes with spot GPU instances. Subsequent traffic was routed to the quantized fallback (redwood-13b-v2-quantized), causing subtle output differences and higher token-level hallucination for their eval set. The customer observed the behavior for ~18 minutes and escalated due to production regressions in generation quality.
Impact:
- User-facing: incorrect/altered responses for a subset of requests (affecting ~12% of requests for the route).
- Business: NimbleDocs classifies this as a high-severity regression affecting SLAs for dedicated customers.
- Scope: Single dedicated pool in us-east-1 with canary weight 10% at time of event.
Relevant contexts: dedicated capacity with spot-backed scaling policy, route-level version pin applied by customer via the API, canary weight adjustments in place, automatic fallback policy enabled to use quantized variants under capacity pressure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have a dedicated GPU pool configured with spot-backed worker autoscaling and canary pool of 2 replicas.
2) Create a route with model pin to redwood-13b-v2 and enable automatic fallback to the quantized variant.
3) Shift canary weight to 10% and trigger a simulated spot eviction on one canary node (drain + terminate).
4) Observe routing decisions and route metadata via /admin/routes and traffic logs; check if pin is preserved when the canary instance set changes.
logs: 2026-03-01T09:14:32Z - scheduler: initiated scale-down of canary-replica-2 due to spot-eviction; draining connections
2026-03-01T09:15:07Z - agent(us-east-1-canary-2): health check failed during replacement; node replaced with spot-gpu-4
2026-03-01T09:15:45Z - routing: decision for route /api/generate -> fallback to redwood-13b-v2-quantized (policy=fallback_on_capacity_shortage)
Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/srv/route-traffic?var-route=nimbledocs; suspicious spike in route latency and increase in quantized-serving-metric
Sentry event: https://sentry.redwood.internal/issue/56422 - small increase in token mismatch score correlated to timeframe
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: pin metadata is stored on canary node filesystem and was not migrated to replacement node during spot-driven replacement.
Checked /admin/routes state at 09:16: service shows model_pin=null for affected route for a short period (~18 minutes); route metadata subsequently corrected when control plane reconciled.

Control plane logs show a race between node-replacement reconciliation and route-pin persistence: route update event (pin maintained in control-plane DB) failed to propagate to the new agent due to temporary backpressure on the routing service.
Observed autoscaler churn: 2 spot evictions in cluster within 5 minutes leading to increased control-plane load.

Reproduction confirmed in staging with a forced drain sequence: whenever agent bootstrap is slower than control-plane replication, route-level transient unset can occur if the agent queries local cache before full reconciliation.
Customer-supplied evals show small but material output regressions when quantized model served versus pinned float variant.
resolution: Workaround applied: Support used the route API to re-apply the pin immediately (customer accepted) and temporarily increased canary replica count to avoid single-node replacement windows. Engineering mitigation: patch landed to ensure route pin is pushed as part of agent bootstrap handshake and to make pin replication idempotent even under transient control-plane backpressure (PR referenced below). Deployment plan: staged rollout to prod canary (us-east) scheduled 2026-03-04; monitoring and post-deploy verification required. Follow-ups: add unit test for agent bootstrap pin sync and an alert when route metadata divergence occurs for >30s.
